{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Treat U1 through U8 as one software increment and estimate implementation, automated testing, documentation, benchmarking, and integration work.",
    "Use the existing Spring XD architecture and APIs wherever possible rather than introducing a new messaging, deployment, or serialization framework.",
    "For U1, make BaseDefinition metadata reparseable on demand, preserving compatibility with existing module resolution and deployment behavior.",
    "For U2, expose reliable HDFS-write completion through an explicit acknowledgement or completion signal that is distinct from message-bus acknowledgement.",
    "For U3, support a configurable partition function at source and processor module level, with the existing default partition behavior retained when no override is configured.",
    "For U4, extend consumer configuration and runtime handling to subscribe to multiple topic-partitions while presenting a single downstream queue.",
    "For U5, implement a parser that can parse a complete Flo definition or an explicitly supplied symbol/context table, allowing references to streams defined elsewhere.",
    "For U6, produce an architecture/design proposal for single-container stream deployment rather than implementing the deployment model, because the requirement asks to design and document the approach.",
    "For U7, preserve non-default ConfigurableConversionService configuration across tuple serialization and deserialization by carrying or reconstructing the required conversion-service context.",
    "For U8, use a repeatable benchmark scenario with JMX enabled and disabled, recording throughput, latency, CPU, memory, and relevant measurement limitations."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The referenced Spring XD repository branch and its build environment are available, buildable, and sufficiently representative of the target codebase.",
    "The estimate covers one developer performing analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and benchmark execution; it excludes waiting time for external reviews, infrastructure provisioning, or unavailable dependencies.",
    "Existing unit-test and integration-test frameworks, local Kafka or equivalent broker support, and local or mock HDFS support can be reused.",
    "Backward compatibility is required for existing module definitions, partitioning behavior, consumer configurations, tuple formats, and parser callers unless a story explicitly changes that behavior.",
    "Reliable HDFS acknowledgement means acknowledgement after the relevant HDFS commit or close operation succeeds, with failure propagated to the stream-processing path; exactly-once semantics are not required.",
    "U3 requires configuration and extension points for partition functions, not a new partitioning algorithm or a graphical configuration interface.",
    "U4 does not require dynamic partition discovery or rebalancing beyond capabilities already provided by the underlying messaging client.",
    "U5 parser diagnostics need to identify invalid module or option values, but a complete redesign of the Flo language or UI is out of scope.",
    "U6 documentation includes deployment architecture, lifecycle, isolation, configuration, resource, and operational considerations, but not production implementation.",
    "U8 benchmarking is limited to a representative stream scenario and a controlled comparison of JMX enabled versus disabled; exhaustive performance characterization across all workloads is out of scope.",
    "Effort includes normal code review preparation and remediation of issues found during the developer's own verification, but not separate independent QA staffing."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository baseline and increment analysis",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the referenced branch and relevant Spring XD modules, trace existing deployment, messaging, parsing, serialization, and monitoring flows, establish a build baseline, and identify affected tests and compatibility constraints.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Implement BaseDefinition module-list removal and reparsing",
      "activity_description": "Experiment with removing the stored module list from BaseDefinition, implement reparsing or lazy reconstruction as needed, update dependent code paths, and add regression tests for definition resolution and deployment behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Implement reliable HDFS commit acknowledgements",
      "activity_description": "Trace the stream sink and HDFS write lifecycle, add commit-aware acknowledgement and error propagation, integrate the behavior with message handling and configuration, and create unit and integration tests using HDFS test doubles or a local test environment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 14
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Add configurable source and processor partition functions",
      "activity_description": "Define the partition-function extension point and configuration contract, integrate it into source and processor routing, preserve default behavior, validate invalid configurations, and add routing and regression tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 7
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Support consumption from multiple topic-partitions",
      "activity_description": "Extend consumer configuration and runtime subscription logic to accept multiple topic-partitions, merge consumed records into the existing single downstream queue model, handle offsets and error cases, and add multi-partition integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Implement context-aware Flo DSL parsing",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement parsing of complete or separately supplied stream definitions with symbol/context awareness, detect invalid module and option values, preserve existing parser behavior where possible, and add parser and API regression tests for cross-stream references.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Design and document single-container stream deployment",
      "activity_description": "Evaluate module colocation, lifecycle management, communication, configuration, scaling, resource isolation, failure handling, observability, and upgrade implications, then produce an architecture/design document with alternatives and a recommended approach.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Preserve non-default conversion services during tuple deserialization",
      "activity_description": "Trace tuple serialization and deserialization paths, define how custom ConfigurableConversionService instances or configuration are retained, implement uniform handling, and add tests covering non-default conversions and backward compatibility.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Benchmark JMX-enabled and JMX-disabled streams",
      "activity_description": "Create a repeatable representative stream benchmark, control the test environment, run comparable JMX-enabled and JMX-disabled measurements, collect performance data, analyze results and limitations, and document the findings.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and regression verification",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and relevant integration suites, verify interactions among deployment, parsing, messaging, serialization, and monitoring changes, diagnose and fix integration defects, and perform final compatibility checks.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Final documentation, packaging, and delivery preparation",
      "activity_description": "Update user and developer documentation, configuration examples, test notes, benchmark references, change summaries, and delivery artifacts; perform final cleanup and prepare the increment for review.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 84
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Treat U1 through U8 as one software increment and estimate implementation, automated testing, documentation, benchmarking, and integration work.
Use the existing Spring XD architecture and APIs wherever possible rather than introducing a new messaging, deployment, or serialization framework.
For U1, make BaseDefinition metadata reparseable on demand, preserving compatibility with existing module resolution and deployment behavior.
For U2, expose reliable HDFS-write completion through an explicit acknowledgement or completion signal that is distinct from message-bus acknowledgement.
For U3, support a configurable partition function at source and processor module level, with the existing default partition behavior retained when no override is configured.
For U4, extend consumer configuration and runtime handling to subscribe to multiple topic-partitions while presenting a single downstream queue.
For U5, implement a parser that can parse a complete Flo definition or an explicitly supplied symbol/context table, allowing references to streams defined elsewhere.
For U6, produce an architecture/design proposal for single-container stream deployment rather than implementing the deployment model, because the requirement asks to design and document the approach.
For U7, preserve non-default ConfigurableConversionService configuration across tuple serialization and deserialization by carrying or reconstructing the required conversion-service context.
For U8, use a repeatable benchmark scenario with JMX enabled and disabled, recording throughput, latency, CPU, memory, and relevant measurement limitations.
assumptions: The referenced Spring XD repository branch and its build environment are available, buildable, and sufficiently representative of the target codebase.

The estimate covers one developer performing analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and benchmark execution; it excludes waiting time for external reviews, infrastructure provisioning, or unavailable dependencies.
Existing unit-test and integration-test frameworks, local Kafka or equivalent broker support, and local or mock HDFS support can be reused.
Backward compatibility is required for existing module definitions, partitioning behavior, consumer configurations, tuple formats, and parser callers unless a story explicitly changes that behavior.

Reliable HDFS acknowledgement means acknowledgement after the relevant HDFS commit or close operation succeeds, with failure propagated to the stream-processing path; exactly-once semantics are not required.
U3 requires configuration and extension points for partition functions, not a new partitioning algorithm or a graphical configuration interface.
U4 does not require dynamic partition discovery or rebalancing beyond capabilities already provided by the underlying messaging client.
U5 parser diagnostics need to identify invalid module or option values, but a complete redesign of the Flo language or UI is out of scope.
U6 documentation includes deployment architecture, lifecycle, isolation, configuration, resource, and operational considerations, but not production implementation.

U8 benchmarking is limited to a representative stream scenario and a controlled comparison of JMX enabled versus disabled; exhaustive performance characterization across all workloads is out of scope.
Effort includes normal code review preparation and remediation of issues found during the developer's own verification, but not separate independent QA staffing.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the referenced branch and relevant Spring XD modules, trace existing deployment, messaging, parsing, serialization, and monitoring flows, establish a build baseline, and identify affected tests and compatibility constraints.

activities.activity_name: Implement BaseDefinition module-list removal and reparsing
activities.activity_description: Experiment with removing the stored module list from BaseDefinition, implement reparsing or lazy reconstruction as needed, update dependent code paths, and add regression tests for definition resolution and deployment behavior.

Trace the stream sink and HDFS write lifecycle, add commit-aware acknowledgement and error propagation, integrate the behavior with message handling and configuration, and create unit and integration tests using HDFS test doubles or a local test environment.

activities.activity_name: Add configurable source and processor partition functions
activities.activity_description: Define the partition-function extension point and configuration contract, integrate it into source and processor routing, preserve default behavior, validate invalid configurations, and add routing and regression tests.

Extend consumer configuration and runtime subscription logic to accept multiple topic-partitions, merge consumed records into the existing single downstream queue model, handle offsets and error cases, and add multi-partition integration tests.

Design and implement parsing of complete or separately supplied stream definitions with symbol/context awareness, detect invalid module and option values, preserve existing parser behavior where possible, and add parser and API regression tests for cross-stream references.

activities.activity_name: Design and document single-container stream deployment
activities.activity_description: Evaluate module colocation, lifecycle management, communication, configuration, scaling, resource isolation, failure handling, observability, and upgrade implications, then produce an architecture/design document with alternatives and a recommended approach.

activities.activity_name: Preserve non-default conversion services during tuple deserialization
activities.activity_description: Trace tuple serialization and deserialization paths, define how custom ConfigurableConversionService instances or configuration are retained, implement uniform handling, and add tests covering non-default conversions and backward compatibility.

Create a repeatable representative stream benchmark, control the test environment, run comparable JMX-enabled and JMX-disabled measurements, collect performance data, analyze results and limitations, and document the findings.

Run the complete build and relevant integration suites, verify interactions among deployment, parsing, messaging, serialization, and monitoring changes, diagnose and fix integration defects, and perform final compatibility checks.

activities.activity_name: Final documentation, packaging, and delivery preparation
activities.activity_description: Update user and developer documentation, configuration examples, test notes, benchmark references, change summaries, and delivery artifacts; perform final cleanup and prepare the increment for review.
